chapter: Louis Jordan, Ink Spots and the union
title: Musicians' union Local 802 and how it helps
summary: He joined 802 with Duke around 1929, rejoined after 1970, and says the union finds work according to reputation.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: How do you feel about the union, like you've belonged to the union now for a long time.
No, I mean you belonged to 802 before that.
You didn't have to join when you played at the Onyx Club? What about 802, when you were back in
I joined 802 -- huh -- when I joined Duke.
Yeah. I had to be in the union.
So you've actually belonged to the union almost like 48 years?
Well, of course you discontinued I guess around 1970?
Then when I come back out here I had to join over again and pay the same amount.
So anyway, over 40 years. So you must have some opinions about the union.
Well, it's all right. They keep you working. They Say you go down for a job and they've got a job for you, you go ahead to work.
And then if you don't get your own, that's the time to go to the union and find out why you're not working. And they try to find you a job.
And of course they'll find you if they want you to work.
If they want you to work.
Any time they want you to work.
You mean some people are on better terms with them than other people.
Yeah. It's according to the people that they are acquainted with, you know.
You think it's more like musical reputation or more of a social thing?
Who knows what and what's what, you know.
And where the rumor's gone, who's going to be hired and who's in a position to take it. So that's the type of thing that's going on, if it's not going on yet, and I believe it is.
Do you belong to the union?
Not right now, no. I used to.
No? You expect to, don't you?
Yeah, I'll probably rejoin. Like the last couple of years a lot of the rooms I've been playing in are not union rooms, so --
You'll get a better break if you do, I'm telling you.
